passage:
A museum displayed an ancient calendar system based on the moon, seasons, and farming cycles.
Students compared it with the calendar on their phones. The old system connected time to planting, festivals, and sky watching. The phone calendar connected time to classes, meetings, and alarms.
The guide said every calendar reflects what a society needs to organize.
Students realized timekeeping is not only counting days. It is deciding what matters enough to mark.
The ancient calendar made time feel less automatic. Months and weeks are tools humans use to live together. Different tools shape different rhythms.
